PAUSE_INSTRUCTIONS_GAME_TEXT:
Goal: find the differences between the two images.
On the left, as time passes, the memory fades and the image shifts toward its distorted version.
On the right, the correct scene stays unchanged — use it as your reference.
Pinch with two fingers to zoom; drag to move around.
STORY_LEVEL_000_INTRO_TEXT_ID: I recognize this house, but I don't remember why I'm here. The boxes on the doorstep are mine. This isn't a place: it's a memory of mine, and someone is changing it.
STORY_LEVEL_000_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: Someone is watching me, I'm sure of it. I remember carrying that box up to my room: my new computer is inside.
STORY_LEVEL_001_INTRO_TEXT_ID: My room is as tidy as always, but some things aren't where they should be. There are discrepancies. The longer I fail to find them, the more my mind clouds over.
STORY_LEVEL_001_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: Every difference I find puts the memory back in place, but another appears beneath it. Words I never typed show up on the screen: 'Not choosing is a mistake'. Then I remember: I took that computer in for repairs.
STORY_LEVEL_002_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The hallway isn't how I remember it. Something rewrites the details when I'm not looking: the more differences stay, the emptier I feel.
STORY_LEVEL_002_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The memory returns to its place, but I'm afraid. Among the photographs I recognize the sign of the old electronics shop. The mirror, though, gave nothing back to me. Why?
STORY_LEVEL_003_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The shop is closed and the sky makes no sound. Behind the shutter I can make out dead appliances and hanging cables. Here too, things aren't where they belong.
STORY_LEVEL_003_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The windows look normal for an instant. I knock, I call out, I wait: no one comes to let me in. Then the shutter is up, and I don't remember touching it.
STORY_LEVEL_004_INTRO_TEXT_ID: I'm inside, and old computers fill every shelf: they belong to different eras, some older than I am. Only one monitor is on.
STORY_LEVEL_004_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: That computer shouldn't be here, and it shouldn't work either. It feels like a cruel joke made just for me. I watch it.
STORY_LEVEL_005_INTRO_TEXT_ID: This computer belongs to no memory I recognize. The screen is pulling me in... I can feel myself being absorbed...
STORY_LEVEL_005_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: A light erases the shop. I'm no longer looking at an image: I'm crossing through it. On the other side is the house of my childhood.
STORY_LEVEL_006_INTRO_TEXT_ID: This is the kitchen of the house where I grew up. It's as if my memories had sunk deeper still, even though something keeps changing them.
STORY_LEVEL_006_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: I've put everything back in place, and with it returns the calm of an ordinary afternoon. None of these moments tells me why this journey began. The memory moves into the living room.
STORY_LEVEL_007_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The living room is full of light. The old family photographs are here, but their outlines blur. In some of them I see absences that shouldn't exist.
STORY_LEVEL_007_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The memory of cold winters spent playing video games leaves me with warmth and nostalgia. I find myself in my own room.
STORY_LEVEL_008_INTRO_TEXT_ID: Here I can no longer mistake the past for a dream. Every difference alters a piece of my childhood and turns tenderness into dread. The presence grows, feeding on the regrets I've gathered over the years.
STORY_LEVEL_008_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The toys return to their places and the room finds its light again. Am I... reliving my life? Why? Understanding it opens a scene I've never seen before.
STORY_LEVEL_009_INTRO_TEXT_ID: I've never seen this place. Identical clocks show different hours, and none of them is the right one. Here time doesn't pass: it keeps my memories in order.
STORY_LEVEL_009_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The clocks all stop together. An engine, glass breaking, metal. Beyond the arch there's a road, and... Oh no... I'm starting to understand.
STORY_LEVEL_010_INTRO_TEXT_ID: Two broken cars in the middle of the road. I recognize one of them. Of what came afterward I have nothing left.
STORY_LEVEL_010_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: Something serious happened to me in that accident, and my memory still won't tell me what. Of one thing I'm certain: whoever hit me was looking at their phone.
STORY_LEVEL_011_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The hospital bed is empty, and I should be the one lying in it. Beyond the walls I recognize voices. They aren't memories: they're calling me right now.
STORY_LEVEL_011_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: If they're calling me, then my body is still in that room. I try to answer and I have no voice. The light changes color, becomes stained glass: I'm afraid of dying, and the fear carries me into a church.
STORY_LEVEL_012_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The church is empty and its peace frightens me. Every candle reminds me how easily a life goes out. There's no funeral, but I feel it's mine. I never believed in this kind of thing... But it feels so real...
STORY_LEVEL_012_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The doors open and they don't lead to the street. Behind the altar there's a path among the cypresses. I run, and the presence lets me run: it knows where I'm going.
STORY_LEVEL_013_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The cemetery gates are wide open for me. No headstone bears a legible name, but each one seems about to show it. The church was a warning; this feels like an arrival.
STORY_LEVEL_013_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: I look for my name among the graves and I don't find it: I'm not dead yet. That's what frightens me most. The walls close in around me and the escape ends in a room suspended over nothing.
STORY_LEVEL_014_INTRO_TEXT_ID: This room belongs nowhere, and the mirror doesn't reflect me. I can't get out. Here my regrets have a shape: it's the presence that has followed me from the start. It didn't want my body: it wanted my soul.
STORY_LEVEL_014_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: When I call it by its name, silence. There isn't a single guilt to pay for: there's my life, imperfect, but the only one I have. The mirror opens and lets me through.
STORY_LEVEL_015_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The portal drags along objects, rooms, people from every age. My whole life turns around a single center. What does everything I've lived mean?
STORY_LEVEL_015_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: Inside the vortex the noise dies away. A warm light sketches a house beside the water, far from the accident. It's the place I would have built, and I would have called it 'Peace'.
STORY_LEVEL_016_INTRO_TEXT_ID: The house of my dreams stands beside a river. There are no mistakes, no regrets, no hospital rooms: only the simple life I wanted. That's how I know it isn't a memory.
STORY_LEVEL_016_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The dream dissolves without becoming a nightmare. I can't stay here: hiding isn't choosing. The path reaches an ancient bridge, suspended between the earth and the stars.
STORY_LEVEL_017_INTRO_TEXT_ID: Half the bridge is still my world, the other half is lost among the clouds. I'm afraid, but I have to go on.
STORY_LEVEL_017_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The bridge carries me away. Before the end, one last memory is waiting for me, held together by affection and not by regret. They are the faces of friends, and they're looking at me.
STORY_LEVEL_018_INTRO_TEXT_ID: In this photograph there are my friends, our roads, our smiles. For the first time the differences don't distort the memory: they show me how incompletely I had seen it.
STORY_LEVEL_018_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The guilt doesn't go away, but it isn't the only voice anymore. What remains is the love I received and the love I haven't given back yet. The voices in the hospital were theirs. The photograph splits into two lights.
STORY_LEVEL_019_INTRO_TEXT_ID: Two thresholds in the dark. The lit door takes me back to my wounded body and to the people calling me. The dark portal takes me beyond this life. Nothing is chasing me anymore: I can choose.
STORY_LEVEL_019_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: Fear and hope weigh the same. Neither road is without loss. Now I have to decide.
STORY_LEVEL_019_LIFE_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The lit door opens onto the voices in the hospital. I don't know which wounds will stay with me, or how hard it will be to start again. But I have people at my side and a life worth fighting for. The first breath hurts: that's how I know it's real.
STORY_LEVEL_019_DEATH_OUTRO_TEXT_ID: The portal takes me in without erasing anything of who I've been. If all of this is real, then starting over somewhere else can be real too. To those who stay I leave a farewell full of love; there are other challenges and other chances. Then the past goes out, and I open my eyes elsewhere.
